title: The application of AI technologies in STEM education: a systematic review from 2011 to 2021
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in STEM education and asks how AI applications have been used, what STEM elements they interact with, and what effects they have on learning. The authors ground the review in general system theory (GST) to examine AI-STEM as a system composed of subject, information, medium, environment, and technology.

The study is a systematic review of 63 empirical peer-reviewed studies published from 2011 to 2021. The reviewed work spans multiple STEM areas, especially science, technology, and engineering, and includes learners from kindergarten through higher education, though most studies were in higher education. The review identifies six categories of AI applications: learning prediction, intelligent tutoring systems, student behavior detection, automation, educational robots, and a small set of other uses such as AI textbooks and group formation.

The main conclusion is that AI has been used in STEM education primarily to support prediction of student performance, personalized tutoring, behavior analysis, and automated assessment, with most reported studies showing positive effects on achievement, attitudes, motivation, or higher-order thinking. The review also finds that AI is most often implemented in computer-based, face-to-face, higher-education contexts, and that computer system resources are the dominant medium. The authors conclude that while AI shows promise for enhancing STEM learning, more work is needed to better integrate AI with the full educational system rather than treating it only as a technical add-on.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review using PRISMA methods over 63 empirical studies, which supports moderate methodological credibility. However, it synthesizes heterogeneous studies rather than directly testing a single intervention, so it does not meet blue-tier causal evidence standards.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports that many underlying studies found positive effects, but the paper itself does not estimate a pooled effect size or directly demonstrate impact on K-12 science learning outcomes. Because the evidence base is broad and mixed in rigor, the apparent impact is promising but still unclear for the target population.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of AI applications in STEM education, covering learning prediction, intelligent tutoring systems, student behavior detection, automation, educational robots, AI textbooks, and AI-based grouping across K-12 and higher education contexts.
